name: Istanbul
description: Istanbul is a vast, cosmopolitan city straddling Europe and Asia where USD, EUR, or GBP holders enjoy strong purchasing power amid persistent Turkish inflation. Rich food, deep history, and the Bosphorus lifestyle come at roughly 50–70% less than London, Chicago, or Berlin, making it a compelling FIRE-arbitrage base for retirees who want a big-city European feel without big-city European prices.

quickFacts.visa: No dedicated retirement visa; renewable short-term residence permit (initially up to 2 years) requiring health insurance, proof of accommodation, and proof of income (~$620/mo in foreign-currency transfers); permanent residence after 8 years
quickFacts.safetyRating: Generally safe in main districts; petty-theft caution (US State Dept Level 2)
quickFacts.climate: Mediterranean — hot, dry summers and cool, wet winters

housing.description: Modest 1BR on the Asian side (Üsküdar) or an outer European district

dining.description: Neighborhood lokantas and home cooking from local pazar produce

healthcare.description: Basic private care or the public SGK system

transportation.description: Metro, buses, and ferries on a single Istanbulkart

entertainment.description: Tea houses, walks along the Bosphorus, free and low-cost cultural sights

1M.lifestyle: A lean expat lives on the Asian side or an outer European district, shops at neighborhood pazars and cooks at home, and rides the metro and ferries everywhere. Healthcare leans on basic private care or SGK. The Bosphorus here is for walking, not waterfront rent — but the food, history, and street life make a small budget feel rich.

dining.description: Dining out several times a week at lokantas and meyhanes

transportation.description: Ferry commutes, metro, and occasional taxis

entertainment.description: Kadıköy nightlife, concerts, cafés, and weekend outings

2M.lifestyle: A furnished flat in lively Kadıköy puts you in one of Istanbul's best food-and-nightlife districts. You dine out several times a week at lokantas and meyhanes, carry comprehensive private insurance, and commute by ferry. Comfortable and social without stretching the budget.

housing.description: Well-located 1–2BR in Cihangir or Beşiktaş near the water

dining.description: Frequent quality dining at the city's better restaurants

transportation.description: Taxis, ride-hailing, and the occasional domestic flight

entertainment.description: Concerts, galleries, café culture, and weekend getaways

3M.lifestyle: A well-located European-side apartment near cafés and the water anchors a genuinely comfortable life. Frequent quality dining, international health insurance, and occasional domestic travel are all easily in budget — the FIRE sweet spot for Istanbul.

housing.description: Luxury furnished flat in Bebek or Etiler along the Bosphorus corridor

dining.description: Near-daily dining at top restaurants and meyhanes

healthcare.description: VIP private hospitals (Acıbadem, American Hospital) with premium coverage

transportation.description: A car or regular taxis across the city

entertainment.description: Premium nightlife, events, clubs, and frequent travel

luxuryExtras.description: Boat days, weekend travel, and the Bosphorus social scene

5M.lifestyle: A premium Bosphorus-corridor flat in Bebek or Etiler, near-daily dining, and VIP private hospitals define this level. A car or regular taxis handle transport, weekly help keeps the home running, and weekends fold in boats and the city's upscale social scene.

dining.description: Private-chef-level dining plus the city's finest restaurants

transportation.description: Car and driver, plus charters as needed

entertainment.description: Yachting, elite clubs, and a full social calendar

luxuryExtras.description: Yacht charters, art, and bespoke travel

10M.lifestyle: A waterfront penthouse, private-chef-level dining, concierge healthcare, and full household staff. Yachting on the Bosphorus and an elite social scene round out Fat-FIRE living at a fraction of what the equivalent would cost in a Western capital.
